Safety

Trust begins with boundaries.

Reliable intelligence requires more than a correct-looking answer.

It requires controlled execution, explicit checks, honest uncertainty and an understanding of what a system can—and cannot—do.

Hybrid assistant / Current limits

Clear Limitations

Distinguish verified answers, generated explanations and unsupported requests.

Mindscape Epitome uses bounded execution, defined verification routines and explicit capability limits.

Execution scope

Bounded tools.

Python uses a restricted AST interpreter. Host imports, arbitrary files, network access and unrestricted execution are excluded. SQL uses isolated read-only execution, authorizer checks and progress limits.

Result scope

Verification is specific.

Unsupported requests are refused or request missing data. An answer check does not certify every explanation, pedagogical step or general scientific claim. Some checks reuse the same computation engine.

Privacy scope

Local and temporary.

Chats, projects and saved responses live in the browser. Follow-up context lives temporarily in server memory. No cloud synchronization is provided; conversation identifiers are routing boundaries, not authentication.

These are small, targeted Class 12-style task families, often using explicit structured inputs. They do not establish complete syllabus mastery, unrestricted natural-language reasoning or new learning by the native Mindscape model.

Current safeguards and their limits

Execute within boundaries

Generated Python runs through the existing pinned WASI executor, never the host interpreter. Typed inputs reject unknown/private fields and unsafe source.

Read the evidence ↗

Keep scoring independent

Private terminal tests are unavailable to generation. Mathematical teachers and simulator truth judge outcomes after proposals. Successful evaluation episodes do not enter training memory.

Read the evidence ↗

Preserve failed evidence

R5.2 and R5.3 remain failed original campaigns with separately labeled post-hoc recoveries. Recovery does not rewrite gates or replace frozen predictions. Safe checkpoint loading, identity checks and explicit execution modes preserve provenance.

Frozen datasets, model hashes, historical releases and unsuccessful runs are retained. Native neural execution requires MPS and rejects CPU fallback.

Read the evidence ↗

The integration passed independent replay and 108 software tests plus four subtests. Final focused validation passed 15 tests plus four domain subtests. These are scoped engineering checks, not certification, production readiness or proof against every adversarial input.

The two mathematics failures and physics model limitations remain part of the safety and integrity record. Strong execution isolation cannot make an incorrect neural prediction correct.

Learned cross-domain transfer: NOT YET ESTABLISHED.

Execution controls, independent checks, and transparent evidence reinforce one another. Each boundary has to remain enforceable as the system evolves.

EXECUTION SECURITY

A capability-limited environment

Model-generated Python executes in a pinned CPython 3.14.7 WASI guest. The runtime preopens only curated standard-library files and the current disposable task repository, both read-only to generated code. Trusted host tools validate and apply source edits.

Runtime probes deny unrelated file access, sockets, and subprocess execution. Fuel, memory, CPU, output-file size, and host wall deadlines limit execution. If the required runtime boundary cannot be enforced, the system fails closed.

When the documented native macOS sandbox launch was denied and Docker/Podman were absent, the research used WASI. Generated code did not run in the host Python interpreter.

Execute in WASI

Capabilities and resource limits

The host compares private expected values and types after policy termination. A model’s success declaration or exit code zero is insufficient.

EVIDENCE ACCESS

Keep training and evaluation separate

The policy receives the broken repository, specification, and visible tests. Private test inputs, expected values, and reference patches stay outside evaluation-time observations. Hidden terminal tests run only after the policy stops.

Training-only executed teacher trajectories can populate verified memory. Successful evaluation repairs do not become training memory. Working memory resets per episode, and hypothetical planner or dreaming proposals remain distinct from executed experience.

Repository paths reject absolute and traversal names. Ambiguous or escaping targets are rejected; source text is not repaired by the envelope parser. A malformed proposal remains a recorded failure.

Read the coding protocol ↗

SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY

Preserve the record, including failures

Frozen task identities, nested budgets, seeds, and model revisions reduce hidden tuning and duplicate counting. Incremental per-episode saving and deduplication by frozen keys allow resume while preserving completed evidence. Partial rows are not treated as finished runs.

Model, adapter, source, and data hashes; byte-identical original prefixes; raw-to-statistic agreement; and full replay are checked before coverage completion is claimed. Checksum-bound archives and clean-destination restoration preserve the old results.

Unsuccessful trajectories, malformed proposals, operational failures, and earlier negative experiments remain visible. Unknown measurements stay unknown. CPU/MPS precision, batching, cache reuse, individual latency, and diagnostic overhead remain separate.

CURRENT LIMITS

Execution security is a bounded claim

The report does not establish a general harmful-content rate, a semantic hallucination detector, production abuse monitoring, formal security certification, or comprehensive prompt-injection resistance.

The 172 failed coding answers are terminally incorrect programs, not a measured semantic hallucination rate. Agreement on all 400 replayed coding trajectories establishes saved-record consistency, not universal repair success.

The reported SQLite environment limits SELECT-style capabilities, rows, and time, and denies extensions and file access. Its execution boundary does not establish second-domain model learning or transfer.

Credentials belong outside public source and command output. Only bounded research artifacts are included on this site. The archived report mentions security headers for its public deployment; headers for this local preview and any future hosting environment must be verified separately.
